verses.mystical_translation: Hear me when I call, O the Divine of my righteousness: you have enlarged me when I was in distress; have mercy upon me, and hear my prayer.
O you sons of men, how long will you turn my glory into shame? how long will you love vanity, and seek after falsehood? Selah.
But know that the the Living Presence has set apart him that is godly for himself: the the Living Presence will hear when I call to him.
Stand in awe, and sin not: commune with your own heart upon your bed, and be still. Selah.
Offer the sacrifices of righteousness, and put your trust in the the Living Presence.
There be many that say, Who will show us any good? the Living Presence, lift you up the light of your countenance upon us.
You have put gladness in my heart, more than in the time that their corn and their wine increased.
I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep: for you, the Living Presence, only makest me dwell in safety.

contemplative_note: Stillness makes room for truth that noise can hide.
safety_note: The psalm invites self-examination and trust; it does not justify shaming people in distress or claiming safety is guaranteed.
